steps.title: Find the client's documents (three routes, every try logged) and register each one
do: Find the documents the page below lists for this bundle in the client's own folder. Try the routes IN THIS ORDER and record EVERY try, failures too:
1  device: the computer (local drive / OneDrive)    2  m365: the Microsoft 365 connector    3  zapier: the Zapier Office 365 tools
Record each try: python3 {scripts}/run.py access {run} --purpose locate --route device|m365|zapier --result failed|found --note "what you did"
Register each document you bring: python3 {scripts}/run.py doc {run} --role ROLE --file <local copy> --route <the route>   (ROLE is on the page below)
If the client accepted the FNA in full: python3 {scripts}/run.py doc {run} --role accepted_quote --same-as fna_quote
A required document that really does not exist: ask Paul, then python3 {scripts}/run.py doc {run} --missing ROLE --said "Paul's words"
The program checks every file is readable and keeps its text so every figure you enter can be checked against it.
steps.proof: the tries are logged in order and every required document is registered (or Paul said it does not exist)

steps.title: Read the quotes, application, follow-up notes and emails, one page at a time
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py read {run}

The program shows the documents' text page by page. Read each page fully, then acknowledge it with a one-line note (`run.py read {run} --ack ROLE:PAGE --note "..."`). Pages are acknowledged in order; a page with no readable text must be viewed as an image by you.
steps.proof: every page was served in order and acknowledged

steps.title: Enter the setup answers (Step 0b) with their sources; the program checks every figure against the documents
do: Write ONE answers file in the layout the page below describes, every answer with its source, then run: python3 {scripts}/run.py answers {run} --file <your answers file>

The program refuses anything that is not a real option of the template, a reason scenario that is not in the bank, a name, ID or figure it cannot find in the documents' text, and any unresolved conflict between sources (then STOP and ask Paul, quoting both values and their sources).
Never type a figure from memory and never copy one from another client.
steps.proof: the answers are valid, sourced, free of conflicts, and every name, ID and figure was found in the documents' text

steps.title: Show Paul the confirmation table, ask ONE question, record his yes
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py show {run}
Put the whole table it prints in your reply and ask exactly the one question it gives. Nothing is built before his clear yes.
When he says yes, record his own words: python3 {scripts}/run.py approve {run} --said "his exact words"
If an answer changes, run answers and show again: the earlier yes then no longer counts.
steps.proof: Paul was shown exactly these answers and said yes

steps.title: Retirement or Investment only: the client's own reply email with the proposal quoted beneath (one HTML page)
do: A Risk ROA embeds no email: run done email.
Retirement or Investment: write the ONE html page exactly as before (the page below says how) and register it: python3 {scripts}/run.py email {run} --file <the html page> [--base-pt N]
The program refuses a page that does not OPEN with the client's own reply (their address, their acceptance wording) before the quoted proposal.
steps.proof: the page opens on the client's own reply with their acceptance wording, then the quoted proposal (or this is a Risk ROA)

steps.title: The program assembles the data and builds the ROA with the fixed scripts (and embeds the email pages)
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py build {run}

It assembles the data from your confirmed answers (never typed), builds the ROA from the template with the fixed script, and for a Retirement or Investment ROA rewrites the font sizes, renders the email page with wkhtmltopdf, makes the page images and embeds them in the right place. You never edit a script, the data or the .docx.
steps.proof: the ROA is exactly what the program builds from the confirmed answers, and the email pages were rendered and embedded as required

steps.title: The program opens the finished ROA and proves the pre-delivery checks; you look at the pages
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py check {run}

Every line must be a green tick. Then look at EVERY page image it saves (filled fields black not grey; the embedded email pages the same size as the ROA's own text; no image border touching a footer). If something is wrong, tell Paul; never hand-patch the .docx: fix the answers and rebuild.
steps.proof: every program check on the finished .docx is a green tick

steps.title: Save the ROA in the client's ROA & Bus ROA folder, never overwriting without Paul's yes
do: List the client's `ROA & Bus ROA` folder (computer first, then Microsoft 365, then Zapier; record every try with --purpose save) and note the file names already there. Then: python3 {scripts}/run.py name {run} --existing "name one.docx;name two.docx"
If a file with the same name exists the program stops: ask Paul; only with his yes run it again with --overwrite-yes "his words".
Save exactly the file it names, then list the folder again and record what it shows:
python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} save.folder <the folder path>      python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} save.listed_bytes <the size the listing shows>
If no route can carry a .docx, give the file to Paul in the chat and tell him exactly which folder to drop it in; say plainly it was not saved.
steps.proof: the derived name was used, nothing was overwritten without Paul's yes, the folder is ROA & Bus ROA and the listed size equals the local file

steps.title: The final check and the SHORT AUDIT for Paul
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py done {run} final
Put in your reply, as it is: the saved file's name and folder, the .docx in the chat, then the short audit. Nothing longer.
Any red cross means the job is not finished: say so.
steps.proof: the final checker prints no red cross
